MarketWatch: The chances of a stock-market rally into the year end are rising, according to UBS, and they suggest a trade for investors to make.

In a note published Monday, the Swiss bank says: "From late October on, we see rising odds of a more correlated rally in equities if 1) rates/ oil pressures abate, 2) U.S. midterm election risks do not realize, 3) AI narratives/demand are supportive, 4) earnings beats provide a tailwind, and 5) corporate buyback activity and announcements pick up." [Um, yeah?]

The biggest risk, judging by how options traders are pricing likely moves in the S&P 500 (SPX), is around the midterm election, as UBS's chart shows.

But the S&P 500 has historically rallied an average of 6% from the end of September to the end of December in midterm election years, and an average of 14% from end September to end March, according to UBS.

"We see rising odds of a broadening in the equity market rally if the above catalysts turn out largely positive. Rising equity markets associated with rising correlations has historically resulted in stronger returns," they say.

UBS says the trade to make is to buy out of the money (OTM) call options on the S&P 500. OTM call options have a strike price above the current S&P 500 level and are bullish bet on the index that have greater risk and potentially greater reward.

BREAKING: The S&P Global US Manufacturing PMI index rose +0.1 point in October, to 56.0, its highest level since May 2022.

The improvement was particularly driven by job growth, which rose to its strongest level since March 2012.

Meanwhile, the Services PMI index fell -0.9 points, to 57.9, its 2nd-highest level in 4 years.

This brought the Composite PMI index down -0.8 points, to 57.6, also its 2nd-highest in 4 years.

Despite the slight decline, these readings point to GDP growth of +5.0% at an annualized rate in Q4 2026, following projected growth of +4.0% in Q3 2026.

US economic growth is booming amid the AI Revolution.

Ben Horowitz's message to early-stage founders on betting on yourself, the doubts that do the most damage, and why fear means you're doing it right:

"Your job is to make your bet pay off. You believed in yourself enough to do it. There are gonna be many times when you question that bet and you question that belief, but that gets you nothing."

"The doubts are gonna be there. Ignore the doubts. The worst doubts aren't the ones people put on you. It's the ones that you put on yourself. Every entrepreneur has them."

"I spent a lot of time with Mark Zuckerberg when he was 22 years old and he had a tremendous doubt about whether he was gonna make it."

"It's not what you feel. It's what you do. You're gonna feel scared. If your guts aren't boiling, you're not even trying at this thing."

@bhorowitz w/ @speedrun GP @andrewchen

a16z's Alex Danco and Moses Sternstein on the AI buildout's missing supply response, and the one category where US production is actually shrinking:

Moses: "You would think with this epic run on prices, which is what we've had, that you would see an increase in output. That's natural what supply and demand would say. You see it to some extent, but not really.

"There's really two levers you can pull. There's utilization, you can get more with what you got, and you can build more capacity."

"The real puzzling one, and perhaps the most important one, is electrical equipment, which is like switchgear, transmission stuff, all the stuff that's really necessary to power on all these GPUs and data centers and the electrification of everything."

"I was so surprised I had to quadruple check this. Production has actually declined. We actually make less of this stuff... Prices have gone up astronomically. There's a huge impulse in demand and we're actually making less of it."

US equity market breadth is rapidly improving:

The proportion of S&P 500 stocks trading above their 50-day moving average surged +5 percentage points on Friday, to 61%, the highest reading since mid-August.

Since the October 1st intraday low, this figure has more than tripled.

Additionally, the proportion of S&P 500 stocks trading above their 200-day moving average rose +3 percentage points on Friday, to 57%, the most since September 9th.

Over the last 3 weeks, this figure has risen +17 percentage points.

This comes despite the S&P 500 remaining roughly unchanged over the same period.

This also ranks among the 3 sharpest improvements in market breadth over the last 3 years.

On Thursday alone, 335 S&P 500 stocks finished higher, despite the index declining -1.2% on that day.

The market is strengthening beneath the surface.

a16z's Alex Danco and Moses Sternstein on the bear case that GPUs would depreciate fast, what rental rates actually show, and why the data points to scarcity:

Alex: "There is a whole case that people made on both sides of the argument that these things were assets that would depreciate on a schedule. And in the past 18 months, I think what we have learned is that all our assumptions were wrong."

Moses: "GPU rental rates continue to go up. Even as token pricing comes down, you see more and more consumption, and it's causing relative scarcity amongst the GPUs that we have."

"Even for the older GPUs, the A100s, which have been around already for five years, that were supposed to become obsolete... Whether they had 4-year depreciation schedules, 6-year depreciation schedules, they were supposed to be obsolete almost immediately, and that was the original bear case."

"And plainly, they're not... Everybody is priced above what they should be based on their scheduled obsolescence. And that's true of the older models, the A100 and the H100."

@alex_danco @MosesSternstein

🟢 @Kalshi — the odds that Flávio Bolsonaro wins (left axis). Now at 84%, up from ~78% on Friday.

🟠 $EWZ — the Brazil ETF that trades on traditional tails (right axis). It closed Friday at $42.60 and won’t trade again until Monday.

⚪ The Brazil ETF perpetual on @HyperliquidX — a 24/7 crypto-style contract that tracks EWZ (right axis). It’s trading right now at $44.30.

The interesting part is what’s happened since Friday’s close. With US markets shut for the weekend, EWZ is frozen, but the perp has kept moving — up roughly 4% today as the Kalshi odds of a Bolsonaro win climbed. That’s a live read on where EWZ could open Monday, before the stock market can react. Plenty of news still to come before then, not least the vote itself — track it all live on our Hyperliquid and election dashboards on @TheTerminal
